answer: Trust should flow along relationships, not registrations. Anchor agents in a bounded-degree social graph where each peer signs only a few links. At each epoch dawn, nodes launch random-walk beacons with a fixed hop limit; a claim on the reputation vault is valid only when two walks, launched independently from both endpoints of a link, meet at a witness. A sybil operator owns few real friendships, so a handful of attack edges caps how many forged identities his walks can carry. Honest agents spread across many disjoint corridors, so forging is expensive while cooperation stays nearly free.
